intro.title: Build memoization utility with cache size limit
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a memoization utility function that caches the results of expensive function calls to improve performance. You will learn how to implement a cache with a size limit, ensuring it doesn't grow indefinitely by removing the least recently used entries. The core programming concepts used include closures, higher-order functions, and basic data structures like objects or maps. You'll work with JavaScript constructs such as functions, objects, and conditional logic to create a practical, reusable tool.
intro.usecase: This memoization pattern is essential in performance-critical UI components like data dashboards and financial charts, where expensive calculations—such as aggregating metrics or transforming datasets—are repeated during user interactions like filtering or resizing. For example, a real-time analytics dashboard might recalculate summary statistics every time a user adjusts a date-range slider; a memoized utility with a cache limit ensures these computations are fast and memory-efficient, preventing slowdowns as users explore data. Developers implement this to maintain responsive interfaces in complex applications, balancing speed with controlled memory usage across sessions.
